cleanIntro: ⛔ DO NOT STRIP THIS RIFLE MORE OFTEN THAN YOU NEED TO. Zastava say it in as many words — frequent stripping wears the parts — and on a military anti-materiel rifle that is a design statement, not a hint. The published strip is short: bolt out on the bolt stop, and the bolt itself apart against the firing spring. Work on a bench or a clean rug, and do not let the parts strike one another.

steps.title: Empty it and CHECK it before a single part moves
steps.action: The rifle is emptied and checked before stripping — Zastava make that the precondition of the whole section rather than a step inside it. Work on a table or bench, or on a clean rug in the field, and handle the parts so they do not strike one another.
steps.aside: ⚠ The word printed on the page is "rifle"; this PDF's fi ligature has no Unicode mapping, so the extraction reads "rile". The quote is left exactly as the cache holds it rather than silently corrected.
steps.quote:
Before stripping 
the rile must be emptied and checked for that.
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 3. STRIPPING AND ASSEMBLING OF THE RIFLE

steps.title: ⛔ Strip it as little as you can get away with
steps.action: Zastava's own instruction, and it runs against the habit most owners bring from sporting rifles: frequent stripping is harmful because it leads to sooner wear of parts. Strip for inspection, cleaning, lubrication, replacement or repair — not as a ritual after every range trip.
steps.quote:
Frequent 
stripping is harmful because it leads to sooner wear of parts.
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 3. STRIPPING AND ASSEMBLING OF THE RIFLE

steps.title: Rifle on its bipod, thumb on the bolt stop, bolt out
steps.action: Rest the rifle on its bipod. Press the bolt stop with your left thumb and open and withdraw the bolt with your right hand. That is the whole of the receiver side of the strip — nothing else comes off.
steps.quote:
take the bolt out by pressing upon the bolt stop with the 
left hand thumb and opening and taking the bolt out with the 
right hand.
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 3. STRIPPING AND ASSEMBLING OF THE RIFLE

steps.title: Bolt apart: rest the nest on WOOD, press the guide, turn it 90° right
steps.action: Separate the firing spring coupling with the bolt nest resting on a wooden object — wood, so the nest is not marked. Hold the bolt body in your left hand with your thumb retaining the handle, press the firing pin guide with your right and turn it ninety degrees to the RIGHT to disengage it from the bolt body. Then release the spring pressure GRADUALLY and take the spring and the striker out.
steps.caution:
releasing gradually the pressure of the iring spring, take the 
iring spring and the striker out of the bolt body.
steps.quote:
press the iring pin guide with the right hand and turn 
it right by 90° whereby it gets disengaged from the bolt body;
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 3. STRIPPING AND ASSEMBLING OF THE RIFLE

steps.title: ⛔ And that is the limit — the rest is expert work
steps.action: The bolt apart is where the owner's procedure ends. Zastava's line under the figures is unambiguous: further stripping and assembling may be carried out only by expert personnel. There is no published route into the trigger mechanism, the receiver or the barrel.

steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 3. STRIPPING AND ASSEMBLING OF THE RIFLE

steps.title: Detergent solvent for the soot, military lubricant after
steps.action: Zastava name the materials by class: a detergent solvent for powder soot, a standard military lubricant for the parts after cleaning, clean soft rags or specially packed cotton-paper fibre kept away from dust, and a lubrication brush for the barrel bore and the cartridge chamber. Their own product names are given with an explicit "or any equivalent", so you are not tied to them.
steps.aside:
clean, soft rages or cotton-paper iber-specially packed for 
protection from dirt and dust;
steps.quote: Lubrication brush for barrel bore and cartridge chamber.
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 2. CLEANING AND LUBRICATION

steps.title: Check the cleaning is DONE before anything is assembled or oiled
steps.action: Zastava's inspection sequence is an order, not a list: determine how far the rifle needs stripping, check the accessories and the quality of the cleaning material, check the cleaning is properly done BEFORE assembling and lubricating, and only then check the lubrication. Oil over fouling is how a bore is ruined quietly.
steps.quote:
to check whether cleaning is well done before assembling 
and lubrication;
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 2. CLEANING AND LUBRICATION

steps.title: Special conditions mean MORE often, not the same
steps.action: Kept in the open, at low or high temperatures, in humid or sandy country, the rifle gets its inspection, cleaning and lubrication more often — Zastava say so directly. Kept indoors, it belongs somewhere dry and away from fire, a furnace or other heating.
steps.quote:
When 
keeping the rile under special conditions, the inspection, 
cleaning and lubrication should be carried out more often.
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 1. KEEPING THE  BLACK ARROW RIFLE

steps.title: Striker lug into the groove, then the spring, guide turned LEFT 90°
steps.action: Reassembly reverses the strip and the direction of the turn reverses with it. Put the striker into the bolt body so its lug enters the groove on the body. Bring the bolt vertical with the nest resting on wood, press the firing spring guide down into position, and turn it ninety degrees to the LEFT to engage it.
steps.aside:
Then 
turn the guide to the left by 90° so that it is engaged to the 
bolt body.
steps.quote:

on the bolt body,

steps.title: ⛔ THE OPTICAL SIGHT IS NOT IN THIS BOOK
steps.action: This manual bounds itself, and the bound matters on a rifle that is bought for its glass. Reticle position is not an owner adjustment on the M93: it is changed by a GUNSMITH, with a special tool that comes in the accessories, and it is done "according to the instruction for adjusting accuracy of the optical sight" — a SEPARATE manual that is not this book, and one this book does not reproduce. What this book does give you is the acceptance standard and the click value: shots must not deviate from the sighting point by more than 70 mm vertically and 50 mm laterally, and each click moves the hit 10 mm at 100 m. ⚠ If your group is out, the cause is found FIRST and the accuracy check repeated — the reticle is the last thing to move, not the first.
steps.caution: Each shift (click) changes position of the hit by 10 mm when
steps.quote:
special tool contained in the accessories according to the 
instruction for adjusting accuracy of the optical sight.
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 9. CHECK OF RIFLE FIRING ACCURACY AND ITS ADJUSTMENT FOR ACCURATE FIRING, printed p.26

steps.title: Prove the bolt runs, the stop holds, and the striker cocks
steps.action: Zastava's own pre-use inspection, and it is a good function check: the bolt must move freely along the receiver grooves by hand and the bolt stop must hold it at the rearmost position. Then the trigger — the striker must cock as the bolt goes back, and must go forward hard when the trigger is pulled. Hold the trigger back while you cycle the bolt and the striker stays cocked; it will only release when the trigger is let go and pulled again.
steps.quote:
When pulling the 
bolt with the hand backward it must move freely along the 
grooves of the receiver. The bolt stop must retain the bolt in 
the rearmost position.
steps.cite: Zastava M93 Black Arrow Owner's Manual and Safety Information — M93-Black-Arrow-manual-ZA-USA (the file Zastava Arms USA publishes); no edition code printed — 1. PREPARING THE RIFLE FOR USE

deepAbsentReason: The strip in the guided clean above is Zastava's "incomplete stripping", and it is the whole of what this book publishes for an owner: bolt out, bolt apart, and stop. The limit is printed under the figures — further stripping and assembling may be carried out only by expert personnel — and the warranty says the same thing from the other side, that altering the rifle voids it and that servicing goes to an authorised shop rather than to the manufacturer direct. ⚠ AND THE BOOK'S OWN FRAME IS MILITARY, WHICH IS WORTH KNOWING: its maintenance chapter is written around daily and weekly inspections "controlled by the commander of the section", with anything past basic maintenance going to a technical maintenance department. The civilian equivalent of that department is a gunsmith, and it is where the next operation belongs. Nothing deeper is presented here and none has been invented.

reassembly: Striker into the bolt body with its lug in the groove on the body.
Bolt vertical, nest resting on a WOODEN object, firing spring pressed into place.

Bolt back into the receiver; bolt stop confirmed to hold it at the rear.
Barrel bore dry-rubbed and the ammunition inspected before use.
fncheck: Empty and reassembled: pull the bolt back by hand and feel it run freely along the receiver grooves; the bolt stop must hold it at the rear. Check the striker cocks as the bolt goes back and falls hard on the trigger. Hold the trigger back and cycle the bolt — the striker should stay cocked, and release only when the trigger is let go and pulled again. Dry-rub the bore before the rifle is used.
